lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1648: a fourth ring, and the list that made it a 30-site edit

Owner: "we need to be able to wear up to four rings at a time."

Adding `ring4` to PlayerEquipped was ONE line. The other thirty were the
work, and they are why this is an OTA rather than a one-liner: the literal
`['ring', 'ring2', 'ring3']` had been written out BY HAND across 13 files
— the stat sum, the AC sum, hpBreakdown, the fallen ledger, the revenant
loot priority, two fuse-protection id lists, the vendor repair list, the
drop guard, the equip router, and four separate sites in InventoryScreen.

Every one of them had to agree. A single missed list is a ring that is
worn but not counted, or counted but not droppable, or greyed out in the
UI while the equip router is perfectly willing to fill it. So the list
moved to `RING_SLOTS` / `RING_ID_KEYS` / `MAX_RINGS` in equipment.ts and
all 30 sites read it. A fifth ring is now one edit.

  • The equip router walks RING_SLOTS and takes the first empty slot, so a
    new ring goes on the next free finger; only when all four are full
    does it displace the first. The if-chain it replaces would have needed
    a new branch per ring.
  • InventoryScreen's "slot is full" test reads RING_SLOTS rather than a
    literal 3 — a hard-coded count there would grey out the fourth finger
    the router would happily fill.
  • The backfill spreads from the constants instead of naming each field,
    so it can never fall a slot behind the type.
  • ota1648 ratchets that no file writes the list by hand again, exempting
    only the declaration itself — by NAME, not by file, so a stray
    hand-written list elsewhere in equipment.ts is still caught.

⚠ `ring` KEEPS ITS UNNUMBERED NAME. It is the legacy first slot and it is
in every save on every device; renaming it to `ring1` for tidiness would
orphan the ring every existing player is currently wearing. The ugly name
is the compatible one. No migration is needed either way: a save written
before this simply has no ring4, which reads as an empty finger.

Measured after wiring, not assumed: four AC rings worn read
`accessories: 4` and standing AC 14 against a bare 10, and one ring reads
1 — so the fourth is counted, not merely wearable.

Two source pins repointed, both correct consequences rather than noise:
ota991 pinned the death-kit `slotPrio` literal (now spread from
RING_SLOTS; its claim — weapons and armour lead, jewellery trails — is
unchanged and still pinned), and ota1550 counted three `['ring',
player.equipped?.ring…` literals in the triples block. That count only
ever pinned the old three; it now pins the GENERATOR and that it walks the
full list, which is the assertion that survives a fourth finger.

Gates: all 18 green by exit code. Full suite green — 1111 suites /
11435 tests, 0 failures.
